summary: CCC-built stone fire lookout on the highest point in South Dakota, staffed from 1911 until 1967, now a heavily visited wilderness landmark renamed Black Elk Peak in 2016.

facts.design: Three-story stone and wood tower, architect-designed
facts.status_note: No longer staffed for fire detection; maintained as a historic structure within a wilderness area.

access.note: Reached by trail; heavily visited (about 40,000 visitors/year), not rentable or staffed.

visit.trail_note: Reached by hiking trails from several Black Hills trailheads; the tower structure can be visited/climbed by the public.

events.note: Fire detection began on the peak using an alidade.
A 12x12 ft log cabin added just below the summit.
A 12x12 ft wooden cab constructed on the summit.
Present three-story stone and wood tower completed by the CCC (NHLR gives 1938; firelookout.com gives construction 1939-1940).
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, June 13, 1991.
Peak renamed from Harney Peak to Black Elk Peak by the U.S. Board on Geographic Names.

evidence.supports: Highest point in Black Hills; architect-designed stone structure; CCC built over 3 years, completed 1938; ~40,000 visitors/year; last used 1967; renamed 2016; maintained by Custer Ranger District
evidence.quote: It was constructed by the CCC over a three-year period and was completed in 1938. Now located within a Wilderness Area, Black Elk Peak is visited by nearly 40,000 people each year.

evidence.supports: Last staffed 1967, maintained by Custer Ranger District
evidence.quote: The lookout was last used for fire detection in 1967, the structure and its history are being maintained by the Custer Ranger District of the Black Hills National Forest.
Formerly known as Harney Peak, the site was renamed Black Elk Peak by the U.S. Board on Geographic Names in 2016.

evidence.supports: 1911 alidade start; 1919 log cabin; 1920 cab; 1921 enlargement; present tower built 1939-1940; last staffed 1967; highest point in South Dakota
evidence.quote: Started in 1911 with an alidade, a 12x12' log cabin was added just below the summit in 1919. Then in 1920 a 12x12' wooden cab was constructed on the summit, then enlarged to 16x16' the following year. The present 3-story stone and wood tower, built over two years (1939-1940), was last staffed in 1967.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the CCC completed the present stone tower in 1938 after a three-year project; firelookout.com dates construction of the present tower to 1939-1940. Both are given in the story as the tower's completion is described as 1938 to 1940 depending on source.

notes_for_editor: Rapid City Journal rename article returned HTTP 429 on this pass; not used. Height_m 11.0 and precise elevation carried from the existing record, not independently re-confirmed by a new source this round.
